analysis: The PR changes only docs/reference/configuration.md. At head lines 393-395 it adds rows for DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS and expands the DARKBLOOM_CBV2_SOLO_PREFILL_STRIPE row (base line 393). It changes no code, no trust boundaries and no endpoints. The documented prefill chunk, step budget and stripe knobs are local environment variables read by the provider (EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift). Only the chunk and step-token rows say they are forwarded to the LaunchAgent. The operator already controls these inputs (ADV-001 and TB-003), so they add no remote or consumer-reachable surface. The wider Gemma 4 chunk raises KV charges and activation peaks, a performance and memory-admission concern. The doc notes bidirectional media blocks keep 512 and Gemma 4 raises small values to 1120, and says paged-pool KV charges rise accordingly. That is an availability and tuning matter and is not shown to weaken the T-010/T-029 controls. The change does not touch the prefix-cache threat T-041: no TTL, HMAC lookup, salt scoping, disk budget or kill switch is altered, and the SSD cache is not mentioned in the changed rows. There are no secrets, attestation, authorization or encryption changes. Unverified contract: the documented behavior (defaults, clamping, forwarding) matches code that is not in this PR. The code changes behind it, such as the larger Gemma 4 default chunk, memory-admission accounting and the LaunchAgent passthrough list, were not supplied, so the next pass should check that the memory-charging claims hold in EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift and LaunchAgent.swift. The patch excerpt is truncated but the base and head ranges (393 to 393-395) are complete. No findings.
